data.name: Didacus
data.gender_notes: Didacus is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word 'didascalia' meaning 'teaching' or 'instruction'. In Christian tradition, Saint Didacus is a legendary disciple of Saint Hilarion who founded a monastery in Spain and is believed to have lived as a hermit. He is also known for his miraculous ability to multiply food and water. The name Didacus carries the meaning “Teacher” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Didacus usually hope their child will grow to embody teacher and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name symbolizing spiritual instruction and guidance.
data.etymology: Didacus belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Teacher.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Didacus total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_hebrew.name: דידקוס
in_hebrew.meaning: השם דידקוס נגזר מלשון יוונית ופירושו קדוש מוראה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם דידקוס מקורו ביוונית ומשמעותו 'מורה' או 'קדוש'. הוא קשור למילה היוונית 'didaskein', שפירושה 'ללמד' או 'להדריך'. השם דידקוס היה שמו של קדוש נוצרי מהמאה ה-15, הידוע כדידקוס הקדוש, קדוש פטרוני של חולים ומדריכים רוחניים.

in_greek.name: Δίδυμος
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Δίδυμος, ή Didacus στα λατινικά, προέρχεται από το ελληνικό 'δίδασκαλος' (didaskalos), που σημαίνει 'δάσκαλος' ή 'καθηγητής'. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, το όνομα Δίδυμος αναφέρεται στον Απόστολο Θωμά, που ήταν γνωστός ως 'Δίδυμος' (Δίδυμος = δίδυμος, δηλαδή 'δίδυμος' ή 'δεύτερος'). Ο Άγιος Διδύμου, ή Didacus, ήταν ένας Χριστιανός άγιος του 15ου αιώνα, που έγινε γνωστός για την πνευματική καθοδήγησή του.

data.cultural_impact: Saint Didacus is revered in the Catholic Church and is the patron saint of the Canary Islands and the Diocese of Puerto Rico. In some Spanish-speaking communities, he is also considered the patron of cooks and those who work in the food industry. His legend of miraculously multiplying food and water has inspired various stories and traditions, and he is often represented as a monk with a loaf of bread and a jug of water.
data.spiritual_significance: The name 'Didacus' holds deep spiritual significance as it is a reminder of the importance of knowledge, teachings, and instruction in our lives. As a Christian name, it encourages individuals to seek knowledge and wisdom from God and to share that knowledge with others. Saint Didacus's own life serves as an inspiring example of dedication to spiritual growth and self-sacrifice in the pursuit of a deep connection with God. His legend also highlights the faith and trust in God's provision and His ability to multiply what we have, no matter how little it may seem.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Didacus: A name symbolizing dedication to teaching and learning the ways of God. It is derived from the Greek word "didaskalos," meaning teacher. One who bears this name is called to share wisdom and knowledge with others, inspiring spiritual growth.

historical_references.reference: Didacus of Huesca was a Spanish saint who is considered the patron saint of the Basque Province. He was born in the area around 1100 AD and died in 1154 AD. According to legend, he was a hermit who lived in a cave near the Ebro River and performed many miracles. He was canonized in 1672.

Didacus of Alcala was a Spanish Franciscan priest and missionary who was martyred in 1580 AD in what is now the Philippines. He was born in Spain around 1540 AD and is considered the patron saint of the Philippines and of the Archdiocese of Cebu. He evangelized the island of Cebu and was killed by the natives after a failed attempt to convert them to Christianity.

modern_usage.modern_context: Didacus was a sixth-century Spanish monk who is venerated as a saint in the Catholic Church. He is best known for his asceticism, his role in establishing monasteries, and his missionary work. Today, Didacus is particularly remembered in Spain and Mexico. On Catholic platforms, his life and teachings are celebrated through various forms of media and religious activities. In Spain, there are several monasteries dedicated to him, and pilgrimages to these sites are popular among both locals and tourists. In Mexico, Didacus is invoked for protection against illnesses and misfortunes, and his feast day is celebrated on November 12. Overall, Didacus continues to be an influential figure in the Catholic Church and Spanish and Mexican cultures, with a modern context that emphasizes his devotion, missionary work, and the legacy of his monasteries.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Hannah Didacus in Jerusalem, Israel credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Didacus, which means "Teacher". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.
